summary.oneLiner: A PSU bank compounding well ahead of its own conservative guidance

one-line thesis: A PSU bank compounding well ahead of its own conservative guidance — total business ₹6,05,000 crores (+15.53% YoY) on advances +21.18% against a 12–14% credit-growth guide, with GNPA down to 2.08%, NNPA 0.25% and PCR 97.85%. The headline Net Profit of ₹656 crores (+8%) understates the quarter: a one-time ₹1,237 crores DTA remeasurement charge from the shift to the new tax regime absorbed most of a 79.8% jump in Operating Profit, and management says ROA "could have been more than 1%" without it. The two things to hold the bank to are the durability of the run-rate once the ₹800 crores of non-repeating technical-write-off recovery drops out (cost-to-income reverts from 37.49% toward ~50%) and the 40% of the ECL transition provision still to be built before 1-Apr-2027.
financial scorecard (track qoq/yoy): > All figures as stated by management on the call — no ratio has been computed here.
> One-offs that distort the headline (call them out):

> 1. ₹1,237 crores one-time DTA remeasurement charge. The bank moved from the old tax regime (DTA computed at ~35%) to the new regime (~25%) from FY 2026-27 — "this is a statutory requirement… we do not have any option." Total tax provision ₹1,919 crores = ~₹625 crores regular + ₹1,237 crores one-time. Management: "Had it not been there, our Net Profit could have been more"; hypothetically ROA "could have been more than 1% also. That is our rough estimate, but we have not calculated by that way."

> 2. ₹1,018 crores TWO recovery inside Operating Profit, of which ~₹800 crores is from a few accounts "which we don't expect to repeat in the quarters going ahead." This is what pushes cost-to-income to 37.49%; management explicitly says "in the normalized scenario, our cost-to-income ratio will not be at this level; it will further increase."

> 3. Fee income optics. Loan-processing/commission-from-advances fell because renewal charges moved from upfront-and-amortised to an actual basis, and "mostly what happens in Q1 is, sanctions are very less, so renewals are also very less." Offset by "commission from others" up ~70% YoY, largely the ₹55 crores PSLC commission on ~₹2,000 crores of PSLC sold.
> 4. Cost of deposits rose QoQ only because of a reclassification of deposits and borrowings in the international and Indian books — "otherwise, the Cost of Deposits are stable."
guidance (critical — verify next quarter: Management is explicitly retaining the start-of-year guidance despite beating almost all of it, and will only revisit after Q2.

Credit growth: 12–14% retained (actual 21.18%). "We will review the guidance after the 2nd Quarter numbers, because in the midterm, we can review. Immediately within the 1st Quarter, it is not proper to review this guidance… Maybe, hopefully, we can better the guidance further." Endeavour stated: "as a small bank, we should grow more than the industry growth."
Deposit growth: 10–12% (actual 11.28%). With CD ratio at 82%, "we will increase our Deposit growth rates, particularly CASA."
NIM: 2.8–2.9% retained even after printing 3.05% — "our NIM will be 2.8 to 2.90; the guidance will be the same, but we will try to keep it above that only… maybe more than 2.9% slightly."
Credit cost: below 0.75% (actual 0.39% annualised) — "our credit cost will remain within that range of the guidance."
Slippage ratio: less than 1% (actual 0.63% annualised).
RAM share: 62–65% (actual 64.52%) — "We will continue to maintain that share of around 65% of RAM."
CASA ratio: maintained "within the guidance, just below 37%".
Cost-to-income: "below 50% or around 50% only; not much above that" for FY 2026-27 (i.e. an explicit reversal from the flattered 37.49%).
ROA: no formal guidance — "ROA may be at 0.68% today, we see at the year end, maybe slightly near to 1%."
Cost of funds: expected to stay at ~4.36% — deposits fully repriced, supported by borrowings/refinance channels.
Segment growth rates guided: Home Loan 20–25% ("because the demand is there"); Vehicle Loan ~30% sustainable on a higher base (Q1 print was +65% "on higher side due to the lower base"); MSME 19–20%.
ECL: ~60% of the assessed transition-date requirement already buffered; the remaining 40% to be created "in the next 4-5 quarters" before the 1-Apr-2027 transition date.
GIFT City branch: "In the next month we will be opening. We have all approvals in place."
order book & pipeline: Sanctioned-but-undisbursed credit pipeline ~₹15,000 crores — "we have a good pipeline of credit sanctions, that is around 15,000 crores of pipeline we are still holding, which may be disbursed in due course of time after the formalities are completed." (Not hard-dated — deliberately excluded from triggers.)

ECLGS 5.0: "as of yesterday, we have sanctioned around 2,150 crores in ECLGS. Out of these 2,150 crores, we have disbursed around 1,700 crores" — and "this is not even 50% of the eligible customers loan sanctioned under ECLGS," i.e. meaningful headroom remains.

Corporate demand described as broadening: "In Corporate book also, we are seeing demand in working capital availment also. So few limits which were already sanctioned have been availed in this quarter."
Sectors where the bank sees traction: infrastructure and projects, renewable energy, transmission lines, plus "traditional sectors also like steel and cement, ports and other things."
segment / subsidiary detail: RAM (64.52% of advances) is the engine — Retail +27.32%, Agriculture +30%, MSME +18.79%. "majorly the growth is coming from RAM sector where the yield is okay and can be maintained also."
Retail = two products. "In Retail segment, we have majorly two products. Basically, one is Home Loan and other is Vehicle Loan." Home Loan ~+20% YoY; Vehicle Loan +65% YoY off a low base.
Agriculture — Gold Loan called out separately: "particularly in Gold Loan also, we are seeing good growth and that will also continue."

Corporate (~+17%) — no IBPC book at all: "we are not in the IBPC; we don't have any IBPC exposure as of now." The bank is actively "trying to curtail any other low yielding Advances like maybe the PSUs or other government sector companies. That is very, very limited."

Treasury / bond-market arbitrage — corporate loan demand is framed as a bond-vs-loan trade-off: "if the bonds rate is increasing, then of course, the credit rates are cheaper than the bond rates. Then demand… slips into the corporate credit and vice versa also."
PSLC — "we have sold PSLC; PSLC of around 2,000 crores, and we have earned a commission of 55 crores into the PSLC."

Geography — "UCO Bank is now the only bank having head office in Calcutta in the public sector space… We have around 400 branches in the state, controlled by our five zonal offices," against a 3,421-branch pan-India network.
No subsidiaries discussed. The only third party named is channel partner Aditya Birla Money for the UCO 3-in-1 (savings + demat + trading) product.
growth verticals / optionality: GIFT City IFSC branch — all approvals in place, IT implementation in process, opening "in the next month."

Digital balance sheet ₹35,000 crores (from ₹25,000 crores at 31-Mar-2026) across 31 STP journeys; ~70% of fixed deposits are now made digitally ("earlier this was happening in the branches only, physically").
Project Parivartan 2.0 — converting the call centre into a profit centre, with more services offered through IVR and improving fulfilment rates.
RBI ULI (Unified Lending Interface) integration for the STP Home Loan Journey and STP Ashray Loan Journey — "they provide the backend solution and backend validation of various KYC and other things."
CBDC implemented, with enhanced propositions planned; CASA back office and DMS (Document Management Solution) live, supporting the Retail/Agri/MSME credit hubs.

New liability products launched this quarter: UCO Rising Star (children), UCO Gig Scheme (gig workers), UCO Business Aarambh Current Account (startups), UCO 3-in-1 (savings + demat + trading, with Aditya Birla Money).

In pipeline: Omni-Channel platform; Cash Management Service for corporates; new MSME STP digital journeys; GST Smart product ticket size going from ₹25 lakhs up to ₹1 crore; pre-qualified personal loan journey extended to the call centre.
AI: UDAY chatbot "which is based on the AI"; a Customer Delight team created to connect with customers.

West Bengal optionality — "with this change in the regime, we can expect many more… project development aspects coming for our financing. We see many opportunities in infrastructural as well as in industrial aspect… like the steel sector and then maybe railway related sectors and then other infrastructure sectors."
6a. moat & competitive position (optiona: Only PSU bank headquartered in Kolkata, with a dense home-state franchise. "UCO Bank is now the only bank having head office in Calcutta in the public sector space… We have around 400 branches in the state, controlled by our five zonal offices" (of 3,421 pan-India). A structurally privileged position for West Bengal government/industrial business if the state's capex cycle turns.

Very heavily provided book. PCR 97.85%, and 88% even excluding technical write-offs, against NNPA of 0.25% — "So, on the NPA front, we don't have to provide much," which is what lets the bank guide credit cost to stay under 0.75% while growing advances 21%.

Repo-linked retail pricing already at best-in-class rates. "Already we have our best rates in offering for Home Loan and for Car Loan, and we are maintaining those rates… we are not in a hurry to increase that" — pricing power held without discounting, in a segment management says has "no such pressure."
margins & cost dynamics: NIM 3.05%, above the 2.8–2.9% guide, "with the support of lower cost of funds."

Cost of funds 4.36%, down; the deposit-repricing lag from last year's repo cut is done — "most of the deposits have repriced to the latest new rates… the deposits post, I think, will be stable at this level going forward." Non-deposit channels (borrowing, refinance) are an active cost lever: "our overall cost of funds has even declined with the support of lower cost on the borrowings."
Yield on Advances stable ("only 3 basis points"), with the mix defended by shifting away from low-yielding PSU/government advances toward RAM.

Loan pricing environment: retail "no such pressure" (repo/EBLR-linked and stable); corporate — "we have seen improvement in the yield from the Corporate Advances also… We don't see much cut in the pricing as of now in the Corporate segment also." MCLR nudged up 0.05% to 8.80% this month.
Cost-to-income 37.49% is not the run-rate. It falls out of the ₹1,018 crores TWO recovery (₹800 crores non-repeating); guided back to ~50% or below for FY27.
capex / expansion (watch slippage): GIFT City branch — the one hard-dated expansion item: "We are very soon going to open our GIFT City branch. In the next month we will be opening. We have all approvals in place. Our IT implementation is in process." (Watch: "very soon"/"next month" from a 23-Jul-2026 call ⇒ ~Aug-2026.)

IT/digital build rather than physical capex: IVR upgrade, DMS, CASA back office, CBDC, Omni-Channel and Cash Management Service both described as "in pipeline… that will come very soon" — no dates given for these two, so they are not triggers.
No branch-count expansion target, no physical capex number, and no capital-raise plan was given on this call.
capital allocation: No capital raise, QIP or government infusion was mentioned anywhere on this call — no CRAR/CET1 figure was disclosed either. Nothing to date, therefore nothing to trigger on.

Capital is being consumed by growth in RAM and by pre-building ECL provisions: ~60% of the assessed 1-Apr-2027 transition requirement is already provided, "over and above the minimum required mandatory provisions; so we have created extra provisions already," with the remaining 40% to be created over the next 4–5 quarters.

CD ratio at 82% is the binding constraint on advances growth — management's stated response is to lift deposit growth, "particularly CASA," through bundled/digital products rather than to slow lending.
No dividend, buyback or divestment discussed.
risks & watch-items: The ₹800 crores non-repeating TWO recovery. Strip it out and Operating Profit growth, cost-to-income (37.49% → ~50%) and the recovery-driven part of the profit engine all normalise. This is the single biggest QoQ-comparability risk.

ECL transition on 1-Apr-2027 — 40% of the assessed requirement is still to be provided over the next 4–5 quarters. Note the bank has not disclosed the absolute requirement, only the 60%/40% split; the IT model (PD/LGD) is still being built with an IT partner and a knowledge partner. No CRAR impact was quantified on this call.

DTA charge is done, but the regime shift is permanent — future profits are taxed under the new ~25% regime; there is no option to revert ("this is a statutory requirement… we do not have any option").

CD ratio 82% with deposit growth (11.28%) running at roughly half of advances growth (21.18%) — the gap has to close via CASA or advances growth must slow. Retained 12–14% credit guidance may be the bank pre-signalling exactly that.

Guidance credibility cuts both ways — a bank beating a 12–14% guide with 21% growth and refusing to revise until after Q2 leaves the market to guess; a Q2 revision is itself a re-rating event either way.
Concentration in West Bengal (~400 of 3,421 branches, plus the state-capex optionality) means home-state political/economic risk is a two-way bet.
Cost of deposits ticked up QoQ — explained as reclassification; verify next quarter that it was genuinely a one-off and not repricing pressure.

Management said no stress anywhere: "As of now, we have not seen any risk from any sector. As of now, we have not seen any such risk. No stress we have seen." That is an unusually absolute statement to hold them to, notwithstanding the SMA book improving to 0.36% and slippage at 0.63%.
Leadership is interim — the MD & CEO is designated "(I/C)" (in charge) and is simultaneously an Executive Director. Succession/confirmation is an unaddressed governance watch-item.

ECLGS 5.0 dependence in MSME. An analyst explicitly probed geopolitical stress ("this war between Iran and US") on MSME accounts; management denied impact and pointed to ECLGS as the shock absorber — a scheme-dependent answer.
management quality / tone: Confident but deliberately conservative. Saboo presents a quarter that beat almost every stated guide and then refuses to raise the guides — "Immediately within the 1st Quarter, it is not proper to review this guidance." That is disciplined, and rare.

Candid on the flattering items. He volunteers unprompted that ~₹800 crores of the ₹1,018 crores TWO recovery will not repeat and that cost-to-income "will further increase" — he is arguing against his own headline. Same with the DTA: he lays out the ₹625 crores + ₹1,237 crores split rather than leading with an adjusted profit.

Careful with hypotheticals. On the "what would ROA have been" question he gives the estimate but caveats it: "That is our rough estimate, but we have not calculated by that way, because ultimately, this is the situation and this is the final number, which we have."

Evasive on one question. Asked twice where competition is coming from, he answers with a market-expansion narrative; the analyst pushes back — "you have ducked my question" — and the follow-up is still not segment-specific: "we can't quantify as to how much competition I am getting from the private or from the public sector."

Command of detail is good (SMA book to the crore, ECLGS sanction vs disbursal as of "yesterday", MCLR to the basis point), and reclassification/accounting-change questions were answered directly rather than deflected. Small stumble: he answered an ECL question about ECLGS until the ED corrected him.
non-obvious takeaways: The profit understatement is the story. Operating Profit +79.8% versus Net Profit +8% is a ₹1,237 crores tax artefact, not deterioration — and it is a one-time artefact that mechanically reverses out of the base from Q2. The bank is running at a materially higher underlying earnings level than the reported PAT implies.

Two offsetting distortions land in the same quarter and roughly cancel — the ₹800 crores non-repeating TWO recovery flatters the operating line while the ₹1,237 crores DTA charge crushes the bottom line. Neither survives into Q2, so Q2 is the first clean print. Do not annualise anything from this quarter.

The retained 12–14% credit guidance is arguably a liability-side statement, not an asset-side one. With CD ratio at 82% and deposits growing at 11.28% against advances at 21.18%, the guidance is what deposit growth can fund — which is why the guidance discussion pivots straight into "we will increase our Deposit growth rates, particularly CASA."

Provisioning is already close to its ceiling. PCR 97.85% (88% ex-TWO) on NNPA of 0.25% means credit cost is structurally near a floor; incremental earnings leverage now has to come from NIM, fee income and cost-to-income, not from provision write-back.

ECL is being funded quietly out of the P&L already. 60% pre-provided, ahead of a date 21 months away — the "extra provisions… over and above the minimum required mandatory provisions" are a hidden earnings reserve that the market may be reading as weak profitability.

The digital balance sheet grew ₹10,000 crores in a single quarter (₹25,000 crores → ₹35,000 crores) — a 40% sequential move in a channel that is now doing ~70% of FD origination. That is a faster-moving distribution shift than the branch-count framing suggests.
Zero IBPC exposure is unusual for a PSB of this size and means the advances growth is genuinely originated, not bought — the 21% is cleaner than it would be at a peer using IBPC to fill the book.

A "small bank" self-description from a ₹6.05 lakh crore-business PSB ("as a small bank, we should grow more than the industry growth") is how management justifies structurally above-industry growth ambition — worth holding them to at the Q2 guidance review.

All guidance retained unchanged pending a post-Q2 review.

Q2 FY27 → check: the first clean print (no DTA charge, no ₹800 crores TWO one-off) — does the underlying earnings level hold? Is the guidance revised upward at the promised post-Q2 review (credit 12–14% vs 21% actual; NIM 2.8–2.9% vs 3.05% actual)? Did the GIFT City branch actually open in Aug-2026 or slip? Cost-to-income reverting toward ~50%. CD ratio off 82% and CASA growth accelerating. Cost of deposits — did the QoQ rise reverse once the reclassification washed through? ECL top-up cadence and, critically, whether the absolute transition requirement is finally disclosed. Vehicle Loan normalising toward ~30% and Home Loan holding 20–25%. Whether "no stress in any sector" survives another quarter (SMA book, slippage). MD & CEO (I/C) confirmation/succession.

Very heavily provided book. PCR 97.85%, and 88% even excluding technical write-offs, against NNPA of 0.25% — "So, on the NPA front, we don't have to provide much," which is what lets the bank guide credit cost to stay under 0.75% while growing advances 21%.

Repo-linked retail pricing already at best-in-class rates. "Already we have our best rates in offering for Home Loan and for Car Loan, and we are maintaining those rates… we are not in a hurry to increase that" — pricing power held without discounting, in a segment management says has "no such pressure."
margins & cost dynamics: NIM 3.05%, above the 2.8–2.9% guide, "with the support of lower cost of funds."

Cost of funds 4.36%, down; the deposit-repricing lag from last year's repo cut is done — "most of the deposits have repriced to the latest new rates… the deposits post, I think, will be stable at this level going forward." Non-deposit channels (borrowing, refinance) are an active cost lever: "our overall cost of funds has even declined with the support of lower cost on the borrowings."
Yield on Advances stable ("only 3 basis points"), with the mix defended by shifting away from low-yielding PSU/government advances toward RAM.

Loan pricing environment: retail "no such pressure" (repo/EBLR-linked and stable); corporate — "we have seen improvement in the yield from the Corporate Advances also… We don't see much cut in the pricing as of now in the Corporate segment also." MCLR nudged up 0.05% to 8.80% this month.
Cost-to-income 37.49% is not the run-rate. It falls out of the ₹1,018 crores TWO recovery (₹800 crores non-repeating); guided back to ~50% or below for FY27.
capex / expansion (watch slippage): GIFT City branch — the one hard-dated expansion item: "We are very soon going to open our GIFT City branch. In the next month we will be opening. We have all approvals in place. Our IT implementation is in process." (Watch: "very soon"/"next month" from a 23-Jul-2026 call ⇒ ~Aug-2026.)

IT/digital build rather than physical capex: IVR upgrade, DMS, CASA back office, CBDC, Omni-Channel and Cash Management Service both described as "in pipeline… that will come very soon" — no dates given for these two, so they are not triggers.
No branch-count expansion target, no physical capex number, and no capital-raise plan was given on this call.
capital allocation: No capital raise, QIP or government infusion was mentioned anywhere on this call — no CRAR/CET1 figure was disclosed either. Nothing to date, therefore nothing to trigger on.

Capital is being consumed by growth in RAM and by pre-building ECL provisions: ~60% of the assessed 1-Apr-2027 transition requirement is already provided, "over and above the minimum required mandatory provisions; so we have created extra provisions already," with the remaining 40% to be created over the next 4–5 quarters.

CD ratio at 82% is the binding constraint on advances growth — management's stated response is to lift deposit growth, "particularly CASA," through bundled/digital products rather than to slow lending.
No dividend, buyback or divestment discussed.
risks & watch-items: The ₹800 crores non-repeating TWO recovery. Strip it out and Operating Profit growth, cost-to-income (37.49% → ~50%) and the recovery-driven part of the profit engine all normalise. This is the single biggest QoQ-comparability risk.

ECL transition on 1-Apr-2027 — 40% of the assessed requirement is still to be provided over the next 4–5 quarters. Note the bank has not disclosed the absolute requirement, only the 60%/40% split; the IT model (PD/LGD) is still being built with an IT partner and a knowledge partner. No CRAR impact was quantified on this call.

DTA charge is done, but the regime shift is permanent — future profits are taxed under the new ~25% regime; there is no option to revert ("this is a statutory requirement… we do not have any option").

CD ratio 82% with deposit growth (11.28%) running at roughly half of advances growth (21.18%) — the gap has to close via CASA or advances growth must slow. Retained 12–14% credit guidance may be the bank pre-signalling exactly that.

Guidance credibility cuts both ways — a bank beating a 12–14% guide with 21% growth and refusing to revise until after Q2 leaves the market to guess; a Q2 revision is itself a re-rating event either way.
Concentration in West Bengal (~400 of 3,421 branches, plus the state-capex optionality) means home-state political/economic risk is a two-way bet.
Cost of deposits ticked up QoQ — explained as reclassification; verify next quarter that it was genuinely a one-off and not repricing pressure.

Management said no stress anywhere: "As of now, we have not seen any risk from any sector. As of now, we have not seen any such risk. No stress we have seen." That is an unusually absolute statement to hold them to, notwithstanding the SMA book improving to 0.36% and slippage at 0.63%.
Leadership is interim — the MD & CEO is designated "(I/C)" (in charge) and is simultaneously an Executive Director. Succession/confirmation is an unaddressed governance watch-item.

ECLGS 5.0 dependence in MSME. An analyst explicitly probed geopolitical stress ("this war between Iran and US") on MSME accounts; management denied impact and pointed to ECLGS as the shock absorber — a scheme-dependent answer.
management quality / tone: Confident but deliberately conservative. Saboo presents a quarter that beat almost every stated guide and then refuses to raise the guides — "Immediately within the 1st Quarter, it is not proper to review this guidance." That is disciplined, and rare.

Candid on the flattering items. He volunteers unprompted that ~₹800 crores of the ₹1,018 crores TWO recovery will not repeat and that cost-to-income "will further increase" — he is arguing against his own headline. Same with the DTA: he lays out the ₹625 crores + ₹1,237 crores split rather than leading with an adjusted profit.

Careful with hypotheticals. On the "what would ROA have been" question he gives the estimate but caveats it: "That is our rough estimate, but we have not calculated by that way, because ultimately, this is the situation and this is the final number, which we have."

Evasive on one question. Asked twice where competition is coming from, he answers with a market-expansion narrative; the analyst pushes back — "you have ducked my question" — and the follow-up is still not segment-specific: "we can't quantify as to how much competition I am getting from the private or from the public sector."

Command of detail is good (SMA book to the crore, ECLGS sanction vs disbursal as of "yesterday", MCLR to the basis point), and reclassification/accounting-change questions were answered directly rather than deflected. Small stumble: he answered an ECL question about ECLGS until the ED corrected him.
non-obvious takeaways: The profit understatement is the story. Operating Profit +79.8% versus Net Profit +8% is a ₹1,237 crores tax artefact, not deterioration — and it is a one-time artefact that mechanically reverses out of the base from Q2. The bank is running at a materially higher underlying earnings level than the reported PAT implies.

Two offsetting distortions land in the same quarter and roughly cancel — the ₹800 crores non-repeating TWO recovery flatters the operating line while the ₹1,237 crores DTA charge crushes the bottom line. Neither survives into Q2, so Q2 is the first clean print. Do not annualise anything from this quarter.

The retained 12–14% credit guidance is arguably a liability-side statement, not an asset-side one. With CD ratio at 82% and deposits growing at 11.28% against advances at 21.18%, the guidance is what deposit growth can fund — which is why the guidance discussion pivots straight into "we will increase our Deposit growth rates, particularly CASA."

Provisioning is already close to its ceiling. PCR 97.85% (88% ex-TWO) on NNPA of 0.25% means credit cost is structurally near a floor; incremental earnings leverage now has to come from NIM, fee income and cost-to-income, not from provision write-back.

ECL is being funded quietly out of the P&L already. 60% pre-provided, ahead of a date 21 months away — the "extra provisions… over and above the minimum required mandatory provisions" are a hidden earnings reserve that the market may be reading as weak profitability.

The digital balance sheet grew ₹10,000 crores in a single quarter (₹25,000 crores → ₹35,000 crores) — a 40% sequential move in a channel that is now doing ~70% of FD origination. That is a faster-moving distribution shift than the branch-count framing suggests.
Zero IBPC exposure is unusual for a PSB of this size and means the advances growth is genuinely originated, not bought — the 21% is cleaner than it would be at a peer using IBPC to fill the book.

A "small bank" self-description from a ₹6.05 lakh crore-business PSB ("as a small bank, we should grow more than the industry growth") is how management justifies structurally above-industry growth ambition — worth holding them to at the Q2 guidance review.

qoq change log (fill each quarter): Q1 FY27 (this, first note for UCOBANK): Total business ₹6,05,000 crores (+15.53%); Advances ₹2,72,768 crores (+21.18%) vs 12–14% guide; Deposits ₹3,32,315 crores (+11.28%); CASA ₹1,16,136 crores (+12.34%), CASA ratio 36.94%; RAM +25.27% (Retail +27.32%, Agri +30%, MSME +18.79%), RAM share 64.52%; Corporate ~+17%; NII +16.85%; fee income +35%; Operating Profit ₹2,810 crores (+79.8%, incl. ₹1,018 crores TWO recovery of which ~₹800 crores non-repeating); Net Profit ₹656 crores (+8%) after ₹1,919 crores tax = ~₹625 crores regular + ₹1,237 crores one-time DTA charge; NIM 3.05% vs 2.8–2.9% guide; cost of funds 4.36%; cost-to-income 37.49% (guided back to ~50%); GNPA 2.08% (−55 bps), NNPA 0.25% (−20 bps), PCR 97.85% (88% ex-TWO); slippage 0.63% ann. vs <1% guide; credit cost 0.39% ann. vs <0.75% guide; SMA (₹1 cr+) ₹1,009 crores / 0.36% (from ₹1,125 crores / 0.43% in March); ROA 0.68% ann., guided "slightly near to 1%" by year-end; CD ratio 82%; MCLR 8.75%→8.80%; digital balance sheet ₹35,000 crores (from ₹25,000 crores at 31-Mar-2026), 31 STP journeys, ~70% of FDs digital; ECLGS ₹2,150 crores sanctioned / ₹1,700 crores disbursed; PSLC ₹2,000 crores sold, ₹55 crores commission; ECL 60% pre-provided for 1-Apr-2027, remaining 40% over 4–5 quarters; GIFT City branch opening "next month", all approvals in place. All guidance retained unchanged pending a post-Q2 review.

Q2 FY27 → check: the first clean print (no DTA charge, no ₹800 crores TWO one-off) — does the underlying earnings level hold? Is the guidance revised upward at the promised post-Q2 review (credit 12–14% vs 21% actual; NIM 2.8–2.9% vs 3.05% actual)? Did the GIFT City branch actually open in Aug-2026 or slip? Cost-to-income reverting toward ~50%. CD ratio off 82% and CASA growth accelerating. Cost of deposits — did the QoQ rise reverse once the reclassification washed through? ECL top-up cadence and, critically, whether the absolute transition requirement is finally disclosed. Vehicle Loan normalising toward ~30% and Home Loan holding 20–25%. Whether "no stress in any sector" survives another quarter (SMA book, slippage). MD & CEO (I/C) confirmation/succession.
